sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2025-2035 with the Action Plan 2025-2027
sources.organization: Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development of Montenegro
sources.temporal_coverage: National adaptation plan for 2025-2035; cited observed events and social data are dated in the report, while its risk assessment also discusses projected hazards.
sources.methodology: Plan includes sector vulnerability, gender and capacity assessments.
sources.limitations: Local capacity findings are assessment conclusions.

sources.title: Montenegro National Drought Plan
sources.organization: Ministry of Sustainable Development and Tourism, Government of Montenegro, with UNCCD support
sources.temporal_coverage: Plan dated November 2020; it describes then-current monitoring and drought-management arrangements and summarizes earlier events and proposed actions.
sources.methodology: National working group plan synthesizes sector impacts, drought monitoring, risk assessment and preparedness measures.
sources.limitations: Institutional status and statistics are historical to the 2020 plan; recommendations are not verified implementation.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Western Balkans 6. Montenegro Country Compendium
sources.temporal_coverage: Country compendium dated October 2024; combines historical event data, institutional assessment and modeled climate-risk scenarios.
sources.methodology: Uses hazard-risk modeling, a Climate Change Institutional Assessment, and social-protection analysis.
sources.limitations: Model results are scenario-dependent; recommendations describe proposed rather than delivered reforms.

sources.title: Common Country Analysis Update 2023: Montenegro
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Montenegro
sources.temporal_coverage: Light-touch update; the report states its evidence and data are current as of 30 November 2023 and describes 2022-2023 events.
sources.methodology: UN country analysis update synthesizes national and international data across development priorities.
sources.limitations: Climate observations are historical; the update does not establish a climate-conflict causal relationship.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.220, Appendix D, agricultural vulnerability findings on rainfall and water availability.
claims.paraphrase: Projected longer dry periods threaten agricultural water in Zeta, Bjelopavlici and coastal areas.
claims.scenario: Source-unspecified projection within the plan's 2025-2035 period.
institutions: Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development
claims.limitations: Conflict is potential, not observed violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Plan warns of possible tourism-related water-use conflict; same locator.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.220, Appendix D, lowland flood exposure and documented prior impacts.
claims.paraphrase: Lowlands around Zeta, Bjelopavlici, Bojana and Lim have experienced flood damage to crops and infrastructure.
institutions: Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development

claims.locator: PDF physical p.220, Appendix D, 2022 hailstorm impacts in Zeta Plain.
claims.paraphrase: A 2022 hailstorm damaged vineyards and orchards in Zeta Plain; Plantaze estimated losses at €8 million.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.39-40, section 3.7, gender/equity analysis and local disaster-relief information gaps.
claims.paraphrase: The plan identifies Roma and Egyptian women, women with disabilities, unemployed women and older women as climate-vulnerable groups.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.40, section 3.7.1, local budgets and disaster-relief unit information on vulnerable households.
claims.paraphrase: Municipal farm-recovery budgets are limited; local relief units lack reliable data on remote, older, disabled, single-woman and Roma/Egyptian households.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.35, section 3.4.4, tourism-sector vulnerability conclusions; p.37, institutional-capacity summary.
claims.paraphrase: The plan rates climate-adaptation capacity as basic and says coastal and mountain tourism lacks adequate operational risk and crisis plans.
claims.limitations: Assessment ratings are not service outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.48 (printed p.49), section D.3, drought effects on agriculture.
claims.paraphrase: The 2020 plan identifies the coastal and northern mountain regions as particularly drought-vulnerable, with risks to crop yields and farm income.
claims.limitations: Plan evidence and demographic context are dated 2020 or earlier.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.49 (printed p.50), section D.6, social impact of drought.
claims.paraphrase: The plan says poorer communities have less ability to respond and depend on outside support; rural women carry much food-production work.
claims.limitations: The plan does not provide current subgroup-specific impact rates.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.48-49 (printed pp.49-50), sections D.6 and IV, drought vulnerability and institutional arrangements.
claims.paraphrase: The plan described drought management as inadequate in 2020, while assigning the hydrometeorological institute monitoring, forecasting and warning functions.
institutions: Institute of Hydrometeorology and Seismology of Montenegro
claims.limitations: This is the plan's 2020 institutional snapshot, not a current status check.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.94-96 (printed pp.95-97), priority actions on drought governance, monitoring and community engagement.
claims.paraphrase: The plan proposes drought authority and advisory-board roles, clearer warning communication, field reporting and civil-society links with communities.
claims.limitations: These are recommendations in the 2020 plan; implementation was not assessed.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.23 (printed p.11), section 2.1 and Table 2.2, modeled flood risk under RCP 2.6, 4.5 and 8.5.
claims.paraphrase: The report models flood losses above baseline under RCP 2.6, 4.5 and 8.5; the heat-stressor intensity rises in all three scenarios.
claims.scenario: RCP 2.6, RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5; modeled future risk.
claims.limitations: Flood-loss and exposure values vary by scenario and model assumptions.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.23 (printed p.11), section 2.1, historical droughts and local water-resource impacts.
claims.paraphrase: The 2011 drought affected Zeta and Bjelopavlici; 2017-2018 drought lowered Morača and Zeta river and Skadar Lake levels, harming farming, fisheries and power generation.
claims.limitations: Events are historical; the report does not attribute each event to climate change alone.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.30 (printed p.18), section 2.3, social-protection system and climate shocks.
claims.paraphrase: More than 30 social-protection programs cover over half the population, but climate-shock support is limited and municipal disaster aid is often ad hoc.
claims.limitations: The report describes system arrangements as assessed in 2024, not current 2026 delivery.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.31 (printed p.20), section 2.4, municipal preparedness and emergency-management framework.
claims.paraphrase: National, municipal and operational rescue plans exist, but the report says municipal preparedness planning needs strengthening.
claims.limitations: This is a 2024 assessment; the passage does not report municipality-by-municipality readiness.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.9 (printed p.17), environmental-sustainability section on 2022 wildfires.
claims.paraphrase: The report says most 2022 wildfires occurred along the coast and in Podgorica municipality; Montenegro was largely spared in 2023.
claims.limitations: The report records event locations, not climate attribution or impact totals.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.9 (printed p.17), August 2023 extreme-heat observation in Podgorica.
claims.paraphrase: In August 2023, Podgorica recorded its first 24-hour period with temperatures never below 30°C since records began.
claims.limitations: Single event observation; no health-outcome data are given.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.9 (printed p.17), 2022 dry-season hydropower and Pljevlja thermal plant discussion.
claims.paraphrase: Dry months in 2022 reduced hydropower and nearly all power relied on the Pljevlja coal plant, a major air-pollution source.
claims.limitations: The source describes a 2022 energy shock; it does not estimate health effects.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.9 (printed p.17), January 2023 heavy-rainfall and landslide impacts.
claims.paraphrase: January 2023 heavy rain triggered landslides and damaged roads and bridges in Pljevlja, Mojkovac and Rožaje; a person died in Herceg Novi.
claims.limitations: The report does not attribute this event to climate change.

access_audit.locator: Government landing page for the proposed 2025 National Plan for Protection and Rescue from Extreme Weather and Climate Events; 123-page linked PDF is in Montenegrin and its English text search did not surface usable claim passages.
access_audit.notes: Opened the official landing page and PDF, but excluded this proposal from claims because passages could not be reliably read and translated for extraction.

search_audit.query: Montenegro 2025 National Adaptation Plan Zeta Bjelopavlici water scarcity flood vulnerability PDF government
search_audit.outcome: Opened the full government adaptation plan, drought plan, World Bank report and UN analysis; found named plains, river valleys, municipalities and Podgorica exposures.

search_audit.query: Montenegro climate water scarcity possible conflicts over water use tourism agriculture adaptation report
search_audit.outcome: The adaptation plan explicitly warns of possible water-use conflicts under drought and tourism-related supply pressure; no armed-conflict evidence was found.

search_audit.query: Montenegro climate change conflict violence insecurity affects adaptation project refugees report
search_audit.outcome: No directly read primary passage linked violence, insecurity or displacement to interruption of a named climate-adaptation activity; no reverse causal pathway was established.

search_audit.query: Montenegro drought early warning institutional capacity vulnerable groups National Drought Plan government report
search_audit.outcome: Read drought monitoring and warning arrangements, the adaptation-plan capacity assessment, municipal preparedness findings, and social-protection response limits.

gaps: No primary source reviewed established that armed conflict, organized violence or insecurity disrupts climate adaptation in Montenegro; the NAP's water-use conflict statement is conditional and not an observed violence record.
The 2020 Drought Plan's institutional status and group statistics are historical and should not be treated as current 2026 conditions.
The World Bank's Annex C has a figure heading referring to Serbian municipalities despite being in Montenegro's country compendium; that table was excluded from claims pending clarification.
The proposed 2025 national extreme-weather response plan was opened, but its Montenegrin-language passages were not reliably translated for claims and were excluded.
